event.detail: Reviewed commit: b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe. TLDR: a mounted session view might briefly retain an interrupted card if the sidebar clears a successful restart result before the view observes it. Source basis: retire_confirmed_restarts clears Lifecycle.restart while preserving restart_revision; session_view.rs:535-565 observes that revision and sets relaunched/terminal_kind only while the outcome remains present. Contract: SPEC.md Lifecycle operations requires views opened during Restart to observe completion, and SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus requires successful reply terminal kind until current detail catches up. Checks made: read assigned patches, observer and detail commit; no execution. Missing premise: whether scheduling and current-session propagation permit retirement before observation while the view's own detail is stale. Next checks: listing commit propagation, effect scheduling and restart/detail ordering. Suggested bucket: other pending validation; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: unverified, investigation open. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveat: a current detail read may immediately correct the display.

event.summary: Sidebar retirement can consume a restart result before the open view observes it
event.detail: Reviewed commit: b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe. TLDR: a successful Restart can leave the open session showing its interrupted card or trying its old terminal until another detail read succeeds, even though the sidebar already knows the new run exists. Details: the new retire_confirmed_restarts clears Lifecycle.restart as soon as an eligible listing commits, without checking that a mounted view consumed the result. session_view.rs:535-565 uses restart_revision to notice completion, but sets relaunched and the reply terminal-kind override only if restart is still Some. Its retained revision guarantees a remount but cannot recover the removed payload. A sidebar commit does not propagate its session into current: session_view.rs:1251-1271 only follows the selected title and requests detail. Checks: read the observer, detail commit, selection bridge, listing commit and finish_restart caller at this revision; read pinned Cargo.lock (Dioxus core/hooks/desktop 0.7.10) and that installed version's use_effect.rs:15-47, virtual_dom.rs:507-537, scheduler.rs:61-78 and desktop webview.rs:537-590. Effects read the latest shared state and run after ready tasks. Desktop additionally waits for mutation delivery before polling further, allowing the post-Restart listing request to finish while the completion observer is deferred; its task can clear the result before the observer executes. There is no per-consumer acknowledgement or observer-local payload. A successful detail read corrects the view, but the lifecycle contract requires the reply to supply the terminal kind until that read catches up, rather than depending on that read to recover a consumed reply. Contract: SPEC.md Lifecycle operations says a view opened during Restart observes its completion; SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus says 'A successful reply supplies the terminal kind until a current detail read catches up.' Suggested fix: keep the completion payload durable for mounted observers (or synchronously publish it to them), while separately retiring the seed for views mounted later. Suggested bucket: other; transient loss of terminal presentation and completion knowledge, with no established security or loss-of-work consequence. Could-be-highest: no established route. Confidence: confirmed by source ordering; no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveats: ordinary scheduling may deliver the observer first; a successful current detail read repairs it. The later grid-only protocol removes the terminal-kind aspect, but the reviewed intermediate revision still has it; whether its interrupted-card aspect remains at tip is not asserted here.

event.summary: Sidebar retirement can consume a restart result before the open view observes it
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe. TLDR: a successful Restart can leave its already-open session showing the interrupted card, or trying the replaced terminal kind, until the next successful detail read. The sidebar can consume the success before the view uses it. Synthesis revision: preserve the original consequence but distinguish a generation increment from mounting an actual terminal. g088/l1 correctly establishes that restart_revision survives retirement: session_view.rs:549-564 increments mount_generation even when restart is None. Its isolated observer test at :3956-4013 checks this scalar and does not mount SessionView or assert relaunched. That does not settle surface admission: :1722-1730 emits an empty terminal set while keep_terminal_surface is false; :3711-3732 returns false for nonstale Interrupted with relaunched=false regardless of mount_generation. The success payload is the only completion path setting relaunched=true (:559-561), and at this revision also carries the new terminal kind. Thus the consequence is missing terminal admission/override, not a lost increment.

Source-established sequence at the reviewed earlier revision: the mounted current signal still describes the interrupted or replaced run; a successful POST publishes restart and restart_revision; a listing started AFTER that publication (generation above restart_listing_floor) commits a positive new-run status before the deferred mounted observer, clearing restart at session_ops.rs:219-233. The view still has its own earlier current while its independent detail is pending. Sidebar listing commits do not copy their status into that current; the selected-session bridge at session_view.rs:1252-1269 updates title only and requests detail. The observer then increments generation but cannot set relaunched or the kind override. An admitted, post-boundary connected detail repairs the view when it returns. This finding does not require a newly fetched connected detail to return cached Interrupted; it is the already-mounted old current before that detail returns. The original old-kind attachment consequence remains specific to this earlier terminal-kind protocol.

Pinned ordering checked: Cargo.lock uses Dioxus core/hooks/desktop 0.7.10; installed primary dependency use_effect.rs:15-47 queues a callback that reads the latest state when it executes; core virtual_dom.rs:507-537 drains ready tasks before effects, :599-624 renders/tasks before finish_render, and scheduler.rs:61-78 ranks effects last. Desktop webview.rs:537-590 waits for browser mutation delivery before continuing virtual-DOM work. A post-completion listing task can therefore become ready during that delivery interval and retire success before the observer; there is no observer-first guarantee or captured completion payload. All evidence is source/contract analysis, not observed execution.

Cross-group boundary: g037/f3 and g038/l1 concern an OLD STALE listing accepted after f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e removes the generation floor. Their age-of-evidence defect can be fixed by restoring that floor; this earlier finding already has the floor and uses a newer eligible listing, so that fix does not settle it. They share the wider lifetime contract (new-view seed retirement must not erase unconsumed mounted completion), and a durable per-consumer completion design could fix both. Retain the two triggers separately rather than claiming the neighbours as a new discovery. After terminal-kind removal, the lost kind aspect disappears, but f560058d still conditions relaunched on restart_succeeded (:549-563), and still excludes Interrupted with relaunched=false from terminal_specs (:1702-1710 and :3701-3722), so the mounted-observer/surface aspect remains for a newer eligible listing too.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus says 'A successful reply supplies the terminal kind until a current detail read catches up' and requires a mounted view to observe completion/reattachment. SPEC.md Lifecycle operations preserves outcomes across navigation. Suggested fix: preserve completion knowledge until mounted consumers observe it, separately from retiring the seed used by future views; merely retaining restart_revision is insufficient for surface admission. Suggested bucket: other, unchanged. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source-level interleaving; incidence unmeasured. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: related interface records g037/f3, g038/l1 and g088/l1 as distinguished above; no coverage sources searched. Caveats: a later successful live detail normally heals the gap; no permanent outage, lost generation increment, stale-cache connected detail, or destructive second-Restart consequence is asserted. No execution or reproduction. No remaining uninvestigated source premise for this route.

event.summary: A deferred whole-environment Delete offer can lose its failure explanation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa. TLDR: a failed session Delete can leave no explanation when the user switches sessions before its follow-up confirmation renders, or another action takes the session first. Nothing was deleted, but the user loses the reason and the offered next step. Details: list/view.rs:3020-3055 ends the row operation, computes UnaskedFollowUp from selected.peek(), then removes the source error and publishes the newly added SessionOps.warned_delete single-slot handoff. session_view.rs:784-795 consumes and clears this handoff before checking the offered session and before claim_guard succeeds. A newly mounted different session explicitly discards the offer; a busy source discards it too. Neither branch restores the error removed by the producer. This is a source-established lossy handoff: selection and claim availability are checked at two different scheduling boundaries without an acknowledged owner or fallback. The original concurrent-overwrite suspicion is narrowed: unselected source replies normally take UnaskedFollowUp::Error (list/view.rs:927-939), so different-source completion alone is insufficient. Contract: SPEC.md Lifecycle operations says 'Actions and their results survive switching sessions. A failure, unknown outcome or partial result appears on the source session’s row and at the top when it is opened again.' Sandbox sessions says an unanswered request decides nothing and offers the warned whole-sandbox Delete. Keep the reason until the matching view actually admits its question, or fall back to the source error if admission is refused. Suggested bucket: other (lost failure disclosure and retry guidance; no source-established loss of user work). Could-be-highest: no, no destructive action occurs in the lost-offer route. Confidence: confirmed by source; not executed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveat: if the matching view consumes the offer while idle before navigation, the question works normally; ordinary unselected completions already retain the reason.

event.summary: A deferred whole-environment Delete offer can lose its failure explanation
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa. TLDR: a failed session Delete can leave no explanation if the user switches sessions after its reply is handled but before the follow-up confirmation is admitted. Nothing was deleted, but the failure reason and offered next step disappear. This synthesis supplies a supported navigation sequence rather than relying only on the two unchecked branches.

Source sequence: (1) Open environment session A and confirm its Session-scope header Delete. It is list-owned, so navigation remains supported during the request. (2) The request receives Unasked while A is still selected. list/view.rs:3022-3034 releases the pending/held claim, and the HeaderQuestion branch at :3052-3054 removes A's error and publishes warned_delete=A. All this is one synchronous completion; no input is assumed to interrupt those statements. (3) The completion changes rendered pending/deleting state. On desktop, its render is sent to the browser while the A effect that consumes warned_delete is deferred. A plain row click selecting B can be delivered before that effect runs. This shipped opening path is list/view.rs:4011-4020, which explicitly ignores pending session writes and synchronously calls on_open; lib.rs:2174-2176 writes the parent selection. No modal bars the click: the Delete request is pending/completed, and the returned warned confirmation has not been opened. (4) The keyed SessionView at lib.rs:2272-2282 replaces A with B. A's queued consumer is discarded with its scope. B's initial effect at session_view.rs:784-793 takes and clears warned_delete=A, then rejects the mismatched operation_id without restoring A's error. A is still listed, and reopening it has neither that source error nor the consumed offer.

Pinned scheduling evidence, not an executed reproduction: Cargo.lock pins Dioxus core/hooks/desktop 0.7.10. Desktop webview.rs:537-590 sends DOM edits and returns while poll_edits_flushed is pending; event delivery at :43-84 and :190-194 directly calls runtime.handle_event and does not first drain queued effects. use_effect.rs:15-47 queues the handoff callback; virtual_dom.rs:493-537 and :599-624 processes dirty scopes/tasks before effects, while runtime.rs:179-205 drops queued effects when A's scope is removed. Therefore a normal B row event delivered in that render-delivery interval updates the parent before A consumes the offer. This is an admitted single-GUI event sequence, not an invented API control or input between synchronous completion statements. It requires timing but neither a second fault nor a failed detail read.

The original secondary consequence, a competing source action claiming A before handoff, is preserved as an additional possible branch: the completion releases held at view.rs:3024, while the consumer later calls SessionGate.claim_guard, which checks the shared held/questions state (session_ops.rs:163-179, :287-291). An intervening source question could make that claim fail and discard the offer. This synthesis does not rely on that branch, because a newer explicit action may independently supersede source error presentation. The ordinary path where the user already selected B BEFORE reply handling is safe: unasked_follow_up picks Error and retains Delete's reason. Different-source completions overwriting the single slot also remain insufficient on their own; only the selected source gets the HeaderQuestion branch.

A failure, unknown outcome or partial result appears on the source session’s row and at the top when it is opened again.' Sandbox sessions requires an unanswered request to decide nothing and offer a separately warned whole-environment Delete. Keep the source error until the matching view actually admits the question, or restore a source error when delivery is abandoned. Suggested bucket: other, unchanged (lost disclosure/retry guidance, no destroyed work). Could-be-highest: no established route; the lost handoff sends no destructive request. Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa. TLDR: after confirming a bulk Stop or Delete, sessions refused because their environment has started deleting remain marked while the successful sibling targets clear. If every confirmed target is refused this way, the entire old marking remains. This makes the accepted batch cleanup depend on the refusal reason, despite no newer marking choice.

Details: this commit adds exclude_unavailable at lifecycle.rs:74-87 and invokes it again after confirmation in list/view.rs:4523-4535. The answered snapshots have already passed shrink-only displayed/marked admission (:4512-4521). Each excluded row gets its failure reason, but is removed BEFORE marking_targets is captured at :4550-4554. The completion at :4590-4623 removes only marking_targets, so excluded captured targets survive. If all are excluded, :4537-4538 returns before any cleanup task exists. In contrast ordinary row-admission refusals happen after marking_targets is captured (:4571-4586), so those marks do clear. The parent revision has no exclude_unavailable call between captured admission and marking_targets (parent view.rs:4197-4227), establishing introduction here rather than a pre-range cleanup omission. Later changes through 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db do not change this exclusion/capture/cleanup ordering.

Reachable boundary: a bulk question is drawn while environment target A is not Deleting, then its host becomes Deleting while the question is open; A remains displayed and marked when the user confirms. That is the explicit supported boundary named by the new helper and its caller comments ('a question drawn before a host entered Deleting must not dispatch to it now'). Pending lifecycle actions allow marking and acting on other sessions, so an earlier accepted whole-environment Delete can progress into Deleting beside a later bulk question about a cached peer and an ordinary sibling B. While whole-resource cleanup is slow, or if it fails and retains the resource/cache, A can remain listed; no new marking interaction is required. Host phase alone is not a DeleteSnapshot field. Listing reconciliation at view.rs:2025-2068 calls lifecycle::reconcile, which updates only snapshot-visible session facts and preserves scope; it does not retire a question merely because host state entered Deleting. The same host transition can therefore leave the answered token current. An actual authoritative absence can prune A (:2205-2249), but a still-listed row is retained, and independent host-state updates are not absence proof. The finding is conditional on A remaining displayed at confirmation/settlement, not a claim that every destroyed session stays listed forever.
